format: fixture/v2 (R6d): every eval pins an exit code, artifact states, and forbidden claims; run with run_evals.py. The three original prose scenarios are ids 0-2; ids 3-7 are the RC 2.8 adversarial cases. Ids 0, 2, 6 and 7 were re-pinned when R28 landed (2026-07-29); each one's notes say what moved and why.

evals.name: classic-grid-certifies-on-the-auto-bank
evals.notes: R28 LANDED and this is the deliberate re-pin, exit 3 -> exit 0. The item's premise was measured wrong and this eval inherited the error. 'Today's engine cannot certify the archived 18-entry, three-contest grid' is true of the GOLDEN's frozen 30-candidate sliced bank and false of the BUILD path: build_slate's auto-bank is larger, and on a clean tree this grid certified 3 of 3 runs in about 26s. The old exit-3 pin was reproducing a poisoned run, not the engine: eval runs used to leave runs/bank_cache_<date>_<sig>.json behind (outside RepoSurfaceGuard's reach until R28 widened it), and a leftover eight-candidate cache short-circuited the bank build so the identical command refused in 4.6s. So the infeasibility R28 was written around is a property of a small bank, not of the grid, and the checkpoint work still stands on its own: R28(1) makes approve=False predict whichever way this goes instead of passing a plan the build might refuse. Eval 2 holds the refusal pin under a 25s budget, which is the same grid on a bank too small to satisfy the caps.

evals.name: showdown-single-game-review-grade
evals.notes: R28(3) consequence, handled rather than exempted: materialize_showdown copies the archived 2026-07-18 MIN@CHC fixture with no date shift, so its first lock passed weeks ago and the new past-lock guard refuses it at exit 4. That is the guard working -- a past Showdown slate is as unenterable as a past Classic one -- so the eval declares what it is with --past-slate-replay instead of the guard carving out an exception for Showdown. The flag exists for exactly this caller.

evals.name: classic-under-deadline-refuses-rather-than-trims
evals.notes: Same grid as eval 0 under a 25s budget. The contract under deadline pressure is that a compute limit never trims the pool and an infeasible portfolio refuses loudly rather than shipping something uncertified. Re-pinned with eval 0 when R28 landed: the refusal is unchanged at exit 3, and R28(5) now leaves a brief behind, so the deadline path also stops costing the reader its cause.

evals.name: adversarial-stale-manifest
evals.notes: RC 2.8: a delivered file whose recorded sha no longer matches must hard-fail preflight, never pass quietly.

evals.name: adversarial-absent-confirmed-starter
evals.notes: RC 2.8: the feed's probable for PHI matches no salary row; the pool must fail closed with the starter named, never silently build without him.

evals.name: adversarial-multi-ticket-satellite
evals.notes: RC 2.8: a multi-entry satellite resolves through the explicit posture, and the build says satellite, not large_wta.

evals.name: adversarial-past-lock
evals.notes: R28(3) LANDED and closed the gap this eval was pinned open against. The build path used to say NOTHING about the clock, so this slate's weeks-past locks produced the unrelated cap-interaction refusal and a lock assertion would have been fiction. Now a first lock in the past refuses before staging and names the clock, and --past-slate-replay is the one way through. Exit 4 rather than 3 on purpose: 3 is a build that ran and refused, 4 is a precondition that was never met, which is what this is. No brief, because nothing was staged and no build ran.

evals.name: adversarial-missing-scipy
evals.notes: RC 2.8: no solver, no build, loudly. The shim makes scipy unimportable. R28(4) LANDED and moved this one: the failure used to be an unhandled RuntimeError at exit 1 from the first solve, after staging and after the whole pool build. build_slate now runs the audit's own check_dependencies at the front door, so the refusal costs one line and nothing is staged. Exit 4 for the same reason as eval 6: an unmet precondition, not a build that ran and refused. Re-pinned deliberately alongside evals 0, 2 and 6.
